source_name: data.gov.me — Montenegro Open Data Portal
why_relevant: Central catalogue of ME public-sector open datasets; the plausible route to machine-readable registry, tax and statistics extracts without scraping. Also harvested into data.europa.eu, which gives an alternative metadata view.

source_name: Bilansi.me — Montenegrin financial-statement database
why_relevant: Commercial redistributor claiming the first/only complete ME database of filed financial statements with advanced search, company, industry and benchmark analysis. Practical workaround where the tax authority offers no public bulk retrieval of filed accounts.

source_name: Boniteti.me (Dun & Bradstreet / Bisnode Montenegro)
why_relevant: Credit-rating and company-information platform covering reportedly 60k+ ME companies, aggregating registry, ownership and financial data. Useful for ownership chains of vendor subsidiaries and for financials of entities that publish nothing voluntarily.

source_name: CompanyWall Business Montenegro
why_relevant: Free-tier company profiles with financial statements, ownership structure and creditworthiness for ME entities; individual company pages are directly linkable and useful for rapid entity triage (e.g. Razvojna banka Crne Gore profile).

source_name: OpenCorporates — Montenegro Central Register of Business Entities (register #168)
why_relevant: Normalised, API-accessible mirror of the ME company register with documented provenance back to CRPS. Best option for automated entity resolution and cross-border ownership linking where CRPS itself offers no API.

source_name: CompanyData.com — Montenegro legal-entity database (CRPS-derived bulk)
why_relevant: Vendor offering ~92k ME legal entities sourced from CRPS via API/CSV with 50+ fields including corporate ownership. Candidate for one-shot bulk acquisition of the entity spine instead of scraping the registry.

source_name: Schmidt & Schmidt — official extracts from the Montenegrin commercial register and accounting statements
why_relevant: Service that procures certified ME registry extracts and filed accounting statements for named companies — a practical, legally clean fallback when the primary portals are certificate-gated or TLS-broken.

source_name: Državna revizorska institucija (DRI) — State Audit Institution
why_relevant: Audits the annual financial statements of state bodies including Uprava prihoda i carina, and of state-owned financial entities. Its reports reveal the quality, completeness and IT state of the tax administration's financial-statement processing — i.e. how trustworthy the underlying filing dataset is.

source_name: Institut sertifikovanih računovođa Crne Gore (ISRCG) — Q&A and practice guidance
why_relevant: Professional body whose Q&A surfaces practitioner-level detail on filing deadlines, form quirks and exemptions — invaluable for interpreting ME statutory accounts correctly and for spotting entity classes that escape filing.

source_name: PSC — Point of Single Contact for Services (psc.gov.me), business registration & operation
why_relevant: Official EU-services-directive style single contact point describing the full registration and reporting obligation chain for business in ME, including which authority holds which register. Good bilingual pointer for mapping the administrative landscape.

source_name: European Commission – DG ENLARGEMENT: Montenegro country page (enlargement package hub)
why_relevant: Central hub linking every annual Montenegro country report, enlargement package SWDs, Reform Agenda/Growth Plan documents and press material. From here all Chapter 9 (financial services) and Chapter 4 (free movement of capital / payments) assessments are reachable each autumn.

source_name: European Commission – Montenegro 2025 Report SWD(2025) 754 final (annual progress report PDF)
why_relevant: The single most benchmark-dense annual document on Montenegrin banking/payments alignment: Chapter 9 financial services, Chapter 4 capital movement/payment services, AML, deposit guarantee scheme, SEPA/TIPS-Clone commitments, plus forward-looking recommendations for the next 12 months.

source_name: EU u Crnoj Gori / EUME – 'Poglavlje 9 – Finansijske usluge' (EU Delegation & Montenegro EU-info portal)
why_relevant: Local-language explainer and document hub for negotiating Chapter 9 (finansijske usluge): closing benchmarks, negotiating position, state of play, and links to national implementing bodies. Also explains how the EC report is produced ('Kako nastaje Izvještaj Evropske komisije o Crnoj Gori?'), which reveals the national input chain worth tracking.

source_name: European Parliament – rapporteur report on the Commission reports on Montenegro (A10-0093/2025)
why_relevant: Parliamentary scrutiny layer over the Commission's assessment; frequently sharpens or politicises findings on AML, banking supervision independence and financial-sector governance, and signals which reform commitments face EU-side pressure.

source_name: European Commission DG ECFIN – Economic Reform Programmes: Commission overview and country assessments (incl. Montenegro)
why_relevant: Annual macro-financial assessment of Montenegro's ERP includes a dedicated financial-sector section (credit growth, NPLs, supervisory and risk-management reporting frameworks) and explicit policy guidance the authorities must act on — a reliable early indicator of coming banking-regulation changes.

source_name: Council of the EU – Joint Conclusions of the Economic and Financial Dialogue between the EU and the Western Balkans and Türkiye
why_relevant: The ECOFIN-level country-specific policy guidance to Montenegro; the financial-sector recommendations here (e.g. strengthening banking reporting and risk-management frameworks) are agreed commitments that national regulators then translate into law and bylaws.

source_name: EEAS – EU Delegation to Montenegro (press releases and dialogue documents)
why_relevant: Publishes the local mirror of EU-Montenegro economic dialogue outputs and press statements, often in both English and Montenegrin, and earlier than the central Brussels portals index them.

source_name: IMF – Montenegro Article IV Consultation staff reports (Country Report series)
why_relevant: Annual, deeply quantitative assessment of Montenegro's banking system: capital, liquidity, asset quality, cash-loan and real-estate credit dynamics, macroprudential measures, plus a statistical annex with financial soundness indicators. Also flags payment-system integration (SEPA, TIPS Clone).

source_name: IMF – Montenegro mission concluding statements and Executive Board press releases
why_relevant: Concluding statements appear weeks-to-months before the full staff report and already contain the substantive banking-supervision and AML messages; the Board press release adds the official assessment. Best early-warning channel in this cell.

source_name: IMF – FSAP country index for Montenegro
why_relevant: Authoritative index of Montenegro's Financial Sector Assessment Program participation and the resulting FSSA/technical notes. FSAPs are the deepest available third-party diagnostic of supervision, crisis management, deposit insurance and payment infrastructure — low frequency but very high value.

source_name: World Bank – Montenegro FSAP Technical Note on Financial Infrastructure (payments and settlement systems)
why_relevant: Rare, granular independent assessment of Montenegro's national payment system (RTGS/DNS), oversight arrangements, credit registry and collateral registry — the structural baseline against which later SEPA/TIPS/instant-payments moves should be read.

source_name: World Bank – Montenegro country page and Country Partnership Framework FY25-29
why_relevant: Hub for the CPF, project pipeline and press releases; the CPF and DPO operations name financial-sector resilience and EU-market integration objectives, exposing planned reform conditionality before it reaches national law.

source_name: World Bank – Montenegro Systematic Country Diagnostic (and SCD Update)
why_relevant: Identifies structural constraints including banking-sector vulnerabilities, limits of the central bank's lender-of-last-resort function under euroisation, and credit-market frictions — framing that shapes subsequent lending operations and reform dialogue.

source_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports (Montenegro filter)
why_relevant: Machine-queryable archive of every World Bank Montenegro document (FSAP notes, Western Balkans Regular Economic Reports, project appraisal documents) with stable bitstream URLs and an open API — the most automatable entry point in this cell.

source_name: EBRD – Montenegro Country Strategy (2021-2026 and draft 2026-2031)
why_relevant: Country strategies contain an explicit financial-sector diagnostic (bank concentration, SME finance gap, capital-market depth, digitalisation) and set out the EBRD's planned interventions — a forward view of where donor money and technical assistance will hit Montenegrin banks.

source_name: EBRD Transition Report – Montenegro country assessment (annual)
why_relevant: Annual two-to-four page country assessment with transition-quality scores including a 'competitive/resilient' financial-sector dimension, plus a short list of the year's key financial-sector policy developments. Comparable across Western Balkan peers.

source_name: EIB – CESEE Bank Lending Survey (Vienna Initiative), Montenegro country slice
why_relevant: Semi-annual survey of parent banking groups and local subsidiaries covering credit supply/demand, cross-border funding intentions and NPL expectations, with per-country breakdowns for Montenegro. Structured, downloadable data and forward-looking bank strategy signals unavailable from national sources.

source_name: Vienna Initiative (European Bank Coordination Initiative) – reports and working groups
why_relevant: Cross-institutional forum (EC, EIB, EBRD, IMF, World Bank, home/host supervisors) producing working-group reports on NPLs, cross-border supervision, capital-market development and digitalisation in CESEE, routinely covering Montenegro as a host country.
